cards.a: A model that combines on-premises (private) and public cloud into one operational unit, with shared networking, security, and management between them. Workloads and data move between both.

cards.q: Why would an organization choose a hybrid model?
cards.a: To burst into public cloud for spikes, keep sensitive workloads local for compliance, use it as a glide path to the cloud, and for cloud-based DR.

cards.q: What connectivity methods connect on-prem to public cloud in a hybrid model?
cards.a: VPN/IPsec (internet tunnel), Direct Connect (private link), Azure ExpressRoute (Azure), and SD-WAN (intelligent overlay). A secured, low-latency path is the foundation.

cards.q: What must stay consistent between private and public in a hybrid model?
cards.a: Identity (same IdP/SSO), routing (extended subnets), firewall policies (consistent), and management (single control plane).

cards.q: What are the top challenges of hybrid cloud networking?
cards.a: Latency from distance, data gravity (transfer cost), security must be consistent across both, and the overall complexity of operating two platforms.

cards.q: What commands verify hybrid cloud connectivity?
cards.a: show ip route for extended routes, ping and traceroute to cloud subnets, show crypto ipsec sa for VPN tunnels, and monitoring via the cloud console.

cards.q: There is no path to the cloud and high latency. What do you check?
cards.a: Check VPN/link state with show crypto ipsec sa, run traceroute to find latency/distance, verify IdP for authentication failures, and review firewall rules for policy gaps.

cards.q: In hybrid cloud, where do sensitive data and bursts go?
cards.a: Sensitive data stays on-prem; bursts and DR go to the public cloud.

cards.q: Which VPN command verifies the IPsec tunnel in hybrid cloud?
cards.a: show crypto ipsec sa shows the active IPsec security associations for the VPN tunnel.

cards.q: Match the quick review: private, public, connect, burst, compliance, identity, security, goal.
cards.a: Private = on-prem; public = elastic; connect = VPN/Direct; burst = cloud; compliance = local; identity = shared; security = consistent; goal = best of both.
